page.title: How to Choose a Brand Narrative Strategy Consultant
page.description: A practical guide to evaluating, hiring and measuring a brand narrative strategy consultant with checklists, frameworks and decision criteria.
page.h1: How do you choose the right brand narrative strategy partner?
page.definition: A brand narrative strategy consultant is a specialist who audits your current story, defines a cohesive narrative framework and builds a roadmap that aligns messaging across every channel and touchpoint.
page.quick_answer: Start with a paid discovery sprint that delivers an assessment, a prioritised use-case list, a tool choice and a roadmap before committing to a full engagement.

sections.h2: What does a brand narrative strategy consultant actually deliver?

blocks.p: A consultant delivers an assessment, a prioritised use-case list, a tool choice and a roadmap that connects brand voice to revenue outcomes.

ul: Narrative audit across website, sales decks, email, social and event scripts
Core story architecture: origin, tension, resolution and proof points
Message hierarchy mapped to buyer stages and channel formats
Voice guidelines with do and don't examples for writers and designers
Measurement plan linking narrative signals to pipeline metrics

sections.h2: How do you evaluate their process before signing?

blocks.p: Ask for a walkthrough of their last three engagements and verify each stage has a named owner, a tangible output and an approval gate.

ol: Intake: stakeholder interviews, competitive scan, data review
Brief: narrative hypothesis, success criteria, scope boundaries
Production: framework draft, message map, voice guide
Review: internal workshop, redline round, decision log
Approval: sign-off from brand lead and revenue leader
Publishing: channel playbooks, template library, training session
Reporting: baseline dashboard, ninety-day review cadence

sections.h2: What tools and frameworks should they use?

blocks.p: The right partner works inside your existing stack and adds only the structures that reduce rework.

sections.h2: How do you measure if the narrative is working?

blocks.p: Track leading indicators that show the story is being adopted and lagging indicators that show it moves revenue.

ul: Cycle time from brief to published asset
Capacity use across writers, designers and reviewers
Email subscriber growth versus follower growth

sections.h2: When should you hire a consultant versus build in-house?

blocks.p: Hire a consultant when you need an outside lens to break internal consensus; build in-house when the narrative is stable and execution volume is high.

ul: Keep in-house: strategy, brand voice approval and product decisions
Outsource: moderation, member support, programming, onboarding and reporting
Consultant pricing: day rate or fixed project
Agency pricing: fixed build fee plus monthly retainer
Consultant output: assessment, use-case list, tool choice, roadmap
Agency output: working automations, integrations, documentation, support retainer

sections.h2: What does a typical engagement timeline look like?

blocks.p: A first plan runs ninety days: long enough to see a trend, short enough to change course.

ol: Weeks one to two: intake interviews, competitive audit, data pull
Weeks three to four: narrative hypothesis, message map, voice guide draft
Week five: internal workshop, redline round, decision log
Week six: approval, channel playbooks, template library build
Week seven: training session, baseline dashboard launch
Weeks eight to twelve: execution support, monthly review, course correction

faq.q: What is the difference between a brand narrative consultant and a content strategist?
faq.a: A brand narrative consultant defines the overarching story architecture that guides every channel, while a content strategist plans the production calendar, formats and governance for executing that story. The consultant sets the why and what; the strategist manages the how and when.

faq.q: How much should a discovery sprint cost?
faq.a: Expect a fixed project fee for a two to four week sprint that delivers an assessment, a prioritised use-case list, a tool choice and a roadmap. Day rates apply for ongoing advisory work. Ask for a scope-based quote rather than a hourly estimate.

faq.q: Can a consultant work with our existing agency partners?
faq.a: Yes. A good consultant hands off a narrative framework, voice guide and measurement plan that agencies can execute against. They should join kickoff calls, review creative rounds and approve final assets before publish to maintain story integrity.

faq.q: What signals show the narrative is failing?
faq.a: Rising revision rounds, missed launch dates, declining email subscriber growth, low community activation and pipeline that cannot be traced to narrative-tagged content. Review the dashboard monthly and adjust the message map or channel mix within the ninety-day window.

faq.q: Do we need a full-time narrative lead after the engagement?
faq.a: Only if content volume exceeds what a shared producer can manage. Most teams keep strategy and voice approval in-house, outsource production and moderation, and bring the consultant back quarterly for a narrative health check and roadmap refresh.
